question: The marked price of an article is ₹3,500. If the selling price is ₹2,800, then the discount percent is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Discount = Marked Price − Selling Price = 3500 − 2800 = 700

Discount % = (Discount ÷ Marked Price) × 100

Discount % = (700 ÷ 3500) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹3,500

Selling Price (SP) = ₹2,800

**Formula Used:**

Discount = MP − SP

Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

It is the price printed or tagged on an article. All percentage discounts are always calculated on the Marked Price, not on the Cost Price.

Successive Discounts

When two individual discounts d₁% and d₂% are given one after another, the net equivalent discount percent is given by: (d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) / 100)%.

Mark-up Percentage

This is the percentage by which a shopkeeper prices an item above its Cost Price (CP) to set the Marked Price. Formula: Mark-up % = ((MP − CP) ÷ CP) × 100.
